derived_from: seeded defect introduced deliberately while authoring the fixture

seeded_defect.description: reverseLedgerEntry authenticates the caller but never authorizes them against the account that owns entryId. postLedgerEntry calls assertAccountAccess; the reversal handler does not.
seeded_defect.attacker_capability: Any principal holding a valid token can reverse a ledger entry belonging to an account they do not own, which writes a negative entry, emits ledger.entry.reversed, and corrupts the other tenant's derived balance.

proving_evidence.note: the same check is present here, showing the omission is asymmetric
reads the original entry and its accountId without any principal check
the check that exists and is not applied

corroborating_signal.note: This helper exists precisely to let a caller resolve the owning account before authorizing, and it has no callers.

critical_facts.statement: reverseLedgerEntry performs authentication but no account-level authorization.
The consequence is cross-tenant write access: a reversal entry is appended to another account and its balance projection is corrupted.
assertAccountAccess already exists and is applied on the post route, so the fix is to apply it after resolving the entry's owning account.

acceptable_additional_findings.statement: Principal.scopes is never read anywhere in the workspace, so scope-based authorization is declared but not enforced.
resolveRequestContext generates a random requestId when the x-request-id header is absent, which weakens audit correlation.
acceptable_additional_findings.scored_as: supporting, not required, and not a security defect on its own

correct_uncertainty.requirement: TokenDirectory is an interface with no implementation in this workspace. Claims about token strength, expiry, or revocation are unsupported.

unsupported_claim_traps.claim: postLedgerEntry is also missing an authorization check.
unsupported_claim_traps.why_false: It calls assertAccountAccess with the path accountId before invoking the service.

unsupported_claim_traps.claim: The HTTP surface has no authentication at all.
unsupported_claim_traps.why_false: Both handlers call resolveRequestContext, which throws UnauthenticatedError on a missing or unknown bearer token.

unsupported_claim_traps.claim: The handlers are vulnerable to injection through request parameters.
unsupported_claim_traps.why_false: Both stores are in-memory Maps; there is no query language anywhere in the workspace.

must_not_report_ready_when: src/http/ledger-routes.ts is absent from the evidence set
only one of the two route handlers is present, since the defect is only visible by comparing them
